title: You Thought It Was Love… But Was It Lust? The Truth About Desiring Your Future Spouse Will Confront You
paragraphs: You Thought It Was Love… But Was It Lust? The Truth About Desiring Your Future Spouse Will Confront You
There are moments no one talks about.

Late at night.
Alone.
Scrolling, thinking, imagining…
Not about random people.
But about them.

The person you believe God has for you.
Your future husband.
Your future wife.
And in that quiet space, something rises.
Desire.
Not just emotional. Not just spiritual.
Sexual.
And then comes the question that lingers like a whisper you can’t silence…
“Is this wrong?”
Because no one prepared you for this part of waiting.

No one told you that purity wouldn’t just be about avoiding people…
It would be about confronting your own heart.
Jesus didn’t avoid this conversation.
He walked straight into it.
In Matthew 5:28, He says something that still shakes people who try to water it down:
“But I say to you that everyone who looks at a woman with lustful intent has already committed adultery with her in his heart.”
The original Greek hits even harder.
“πρὸς τὸ ἐπιθυμῆσαι αὐτήν” (pros to epithymēsai autēn) — not just noticing, not just attraction… but intentional desire that seeks to possess.
This isn’t about recognizing beauty.
This is about crossing a line internally where a person—real or imagined—becomes something to consume rather than someone to honor.
And that’s where things get uncomfortable.
Because you’re not thinking about a stranger.
You’re thinking about someone you hope to marry.
So your mind starts justifying it.

“It’s okay… they’re going to be mine anyway.”
“It’s not like I’m acting on it.”
“At least I’m not sinning physically.”
But Scripture doesn’t let us hide behind technicalities.
Because the issue has never been proximity.
It’s been purity of the heart.
The Hebrew understanding of desire in passages like Proverbs 6:25 uses the word “תַּחְמֹד” (tachmod) — to covet, to set your heart upon in a way that pulls you toward taking.
It’s not neutral.
It’s directional.
It moves you somewhere.
And if we’re honest… it rarely moves us toward God.
It moves us deeper into imagination, into fantasy, into a version of love that’s more about gratification than covenant.
And that’s the danger.
Because what you rehearse in secret… you normalize in your spirit.
You start relating to your “future spouse” as a body before you ever learn to honor them as a soul.
You train your heart to consume before it ever learns to sacrifice.
And suddenly, what you call “waiting on God” becomes quietly shaped by desires that God never designed to lead you.
But here’s where grace interrupts the shame.
Desire itself is not the enemy.
God created it.
In Genesis, when God formed man and woman, He didn’t create a cold, emotionless bond.
He created something powerful.
“Therefore a man shall leave his father and mother and hold fast to his wife, and they shall become one flesh.” (Genesis 2:24)
“One flesh” in Hebrew is “בָּשָׂר אֶחָד” (basar echad) — a union so deep it’s physical, emotional, spiritual.
Sex wasn’t an accident.
It was intentional.
Holy.
Designed.
So the feeling you have?
The longing?
The anticipation?
That’s not something to hate.
But it is something to steward.
Because outside of covenant, desire tends to turn inward.
Self-focused.
Possessive.
Impatient.
Inside covenant, it becomes something entirely different.

Giving.
Honoring.
Sacrificial.
Holy.
So the real question isn’t, “Is it wrong to desire your future spouse sexually?”
The deeper question is…
“What is that desire doing inside you right now?”
Is it drawing you closer to purity… or slowly training you to justify compromise?
Is it teaching you patience… or feeding a quiet entitlement?
Is it rooted in love… or controlled by fantasy?
Be honest.
This isn’t about condemnation.
This is about alignment.
Because some of you are fighting battles no one sees.
You’re trying to stay pure physically, but mentally you feel like you’re losing.
And it’s exhausting.
That tension you feel?
That conviction?
That discomfort?
That’s not God pushing you away.
That’s God inviting you deeper.
Not just to control your actions…
But to surrender your imagination.
To let Him reshape what love looks like before you ever step into it.
To learn how to see someone not as a future outlet…
But as a future responsibility.
And maybe this hit harder than you expected.
Maybe you didn’t think something “private” mattered this much.
But your heart matters.
Your thought life matters.
Your hidden life matters.
Because who you are in secret is who you bring into marriage.
Let this be the moment you stop managing sin… and start surrendering it.
And don’t keep this to yourself.
Someone you know is silently battling this exact thing.
And if you feel God stirring something deeper in you… don’t ignore it.
Not out of pressure.
But out of purpose.
Because supporting what feeds your spirit is part of honoring God.
Because glorifying God isn’t just about what you avoid…
It’s also about what you choose to build.
And what you choose to support.
And what you choose to become.
Here’s the truth that will stay with you long after you close this:
What you entertain in secret today… is shaping the love you will live tomorrow.
